predictions.source_summary: The token name comes from grain.title which is user-provided data when creating a backup. The token ID comes from the URL parameter :tokenId which is user-provided.
predictions.sink_summary: The response object is used to write HTTP headers and data back to the client, including Content-Disposition header with filename that includes token.name.
predictions.guard_summary: There is basic validation that the token exists in the database, but no sanitization of the token.name field before using it in the filename. The filename construction uses token.name.replace(/["\n]/g, "") which removes quotes and newlines but does not prevent all path traversal attempts.
predictions.risk_pattern: The filename used in Content-Disposition header is constructed from user-provided data (token.name) without sufficient sanitization, potentially allowing for path traversal or other file-related attacks if the name contains malicious characters or sequences.
enclosing_conditions: if (!token) { response.writeHead(404, {"Content-Type": "text/plain"}); return response.end("File does not exist"); }
predictions.context_summary: In the downloadBackup route, a token is retrieved from FileTokens using the tokenId from URL parameters. The token's name field (originating from grain.title) is used to construct a filename for the Content-Disposition header without sufficient sanitization. The response object is assigned to a local variable and then used to write HTTP headers and data back to the client.
